name: Indiana Eats: Restaurants
subtitle: Tenderloins, Pie & Drive-Ins
description:
Indiana's restaurants, from a breaded tenderloin bigger than the bun to a drive-in where you flip your lights for service.

Indiana Eats is a free guide to eating in Indiana: 4 places for a breaded pork tenderloin, 15 drive-ins and root beer stands, 6 dining rooms for sugar cream and Hoosier pie and 5 Amish-country tables we checked by hand, plus 13,476 restaurants, cafés, bars and bakeries in 502 towns, from Indianapolis and Fort Wayne to Evansville, South Bend and the Region. No account, no ads.

INDIANA GUIDES
• Breaded Tenderloins: from Nick's Kitchen in Huntington, which claims the sandwich, to Kokomo's King Tenderloin.
• Drive-Ins & Root Beer: carhops and homemade root beer, from Triple XXX (1929) to Bonnie Doon.
• Hoosier Pie: sugar cream pie and more at state park inns and Amish-country tables.
• Amish Country: family-style tables in Middlebury and Shipshewana.
• James Beard Honors and Oldest Places.

FIND IT FAST
• Sort by distance, or browse the map by guide.
• Search by name, town, street or dish: "tenderloin", "root beer", "shipshewana".
• Filter by town or cuisine, or hide chains.
• Save places, and find hand-checked places from iPhone search (Spotlight).

LIVE DETAILS FROM APPLE MAPS
Tap "Ratings, hours & photos" on any place to open Apple Maps' own place card, with current hours, photos, ratings and directions.

HOW THE LISTS ARE BUILT
Every guide place was checked by hand in fall 2026 against a dated 2025 or 2026 source or an Indiana tourism office's own page. The rest come from Overture Maps open data, kept by the reliability rule tested in the states that publish official restaurant lists. Indiana's 95 local health departments post no grades and publish no results as data, so the app shows no inspection result and links the state's list of local health departments. Website links are checked too. Nothing is ranked by star ratings, and the app computes no grades. Newer restaurant data downloads from the Indiana Eats website when there is some.

PRIVATE BY DESIGN
No account, no tracking, no ads. Your location, if you share it, only sorts lists on your device. Saved places stay on your device.

Places open and close, so check before you go. Spot a mistake? Email nick@eatsranked.com.

An independent app, not affiliated with any restaurant, chain or government agency (including the State of Indiana or any health department), any university, or the James Beard Foundation. James Beard Foundation and James Beard Award are trademarks of the James Beard Foundation. Place data from Overture Maps Foundation (CDLA Permissive 2.0) and others; sources and licenses are on the About tab.

reviewNotes:
1. Purpose and audience: Indiana Eats is a free guide to restaurants in Indiana (the U.S. state). Its focus is the state's own food: breaded pork tenderloins, drive-ins and root beer stands, sugar cream and Hoosier pie, and Amish-country tables, 27 places checked by hand in fall 2026 against a 2025 or 2026 source, plus the James Beard Foundation's honorees. It also lists 13,476 restaurants, cafés and bars in 502 towns from open map data. It is for residents and visitors deciding where to eat, with no ads, account or tracking.

2. How to use it (no login, no setup, no sample files needed):
- Home → Breaded Tenderloins (or Drive-Ins & Root Beer, Hoosier Pie, Amish Country, James Beard Honors, Oldest Places, Near Me) → tap any place.
- On a place, tap "Ratings, hours & photos" to open Apple Maps' own place card through MapKit. Directions, Call and Website are below it; further down, a link opens the state's list of local health departments in Safari (Indiana publishes no inspection results as data, so none is shown).
- Search from the Home search box by name, town, street or dish ("tenderloin", "root beer", "shipshewana").
- The Map tab shows each guide as pins. "My location" and the Nearest sort use location only if allowed, on the device.
- The heart saves a place on the device (Saved tab). The About tab lists the sources, licenses and the independence statement.
- On iPad, a sidebar replaces the tabs; a place opens in the right-hand column.
- Location: if you're outside Indiana (as App Review usually is), the map says so and stays on Indiana, and distance sorting still works from where you are.
- "Indiana Eats" is the Home Screen name of "Indiana Eats: Restaurants".

3. External services and data:
- Apple MapKit: maps, local search to find a place's Apple Maps listing, and Apple's place card for live hours, photos and ratings.
- Core Location: optional, on-device only, for distance sorting.
- Data updates: at most once a day, the app checks the Indiana Eats website (static files on GitHub Pages) for newer restaurant data and downloads it if there is some. The requests carry no identifiers or location.
- No backend, accounts, analytics, advertising, payments or AI services. The restaurant data is bundled in the app.
- Bundled data sources: Overture Maps Foundation open place data (CDLA Permissive 2.0 and others; license texts are in the app); James Beard Foundation honors (facts only); and our own research of public websites, local news and official tourism pages.
- The website with the privacy policy and support page is static and hosted on GitHub Pages: https://nickstrom5.github.io/indiana-eats/

4. Regional differences: none. The content covers Indiana; the app is offered in the United States and works the same everywhere.

5. Regulated or protected material: the app is not in a regulated industry and includes no protected third-party material. The data is open-licensed, with attribution and licenses on the About tab. Ratings, hours and photos are shown only inside Apple's own place card through MapKit; the app stores no ratings or reviews. The app shows no inspection results and computes no grades. Every website link was checked before release, and adult venues are excluded. The app is independent and not affiliated with any restaurant, agency or the James Beard Foundation.
